title: Slow-Cooked Dry Coconut Beef Curry with Lemongrass and Lime Leaf
summary: Beef chuck is simmered low and slow in a hand-blended spice paste and coconut milk until the sauce reduces right down into a dark, clinging dry curry.

ingredients.item: long red chillies, deseeded and chopped
fine sea salt or table salt
makrut lime leaves, central rib removed
lemongrass stalk, bruised and tied in a knot
boneless beef chuck (halal), trimmed and cut into 5 cm pieces

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan) with a shelf set in the middle. Getting the oven to temperature now means the casserole can go straight in once the beef and paste are combined.

steps.title: Blend the spice paste
steps.text: Blitz the shallots, chillies, galangal, ginger, garlic, nuts, ground spices and salt in the food processor for 2-3 minutes, scraping down the sides, until you have a thick paste about the texture of cooked porridge. Add water only 1 tbsp at a time if it genuinely won't come together. Blending the aromatics fully means they'll cook smoothly into the sauce rather than leaving stringy bits of fibre.

steps.title: Combine and bring to a simmer
steps.text: Put the paste, coconut milk, 5 lime leaves, lemongrass and cinnamon with the tamarind in the casserole and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Turn the heat down to low and stir in the beef; it doesn't need to be fully covered by the liquid. Starting this on the hob lets the raw paste cook into the coconut milk before the long oven time begins.

steps.title: Braise in the oven
steps.text: Cook uncovered in the oven for about 2 hours, stirring every 30 minutes, until the sauce has reduced and a pool of oil sits on the surface. The uncovered heat lets liquid evaporate steadily while the beef's connective tissue slowly breaks down, setting the stage for the dry finish on the hob.

steps.title: Reduce on the hob
steps.text: Move the casserole to the hob using oven gloves, as it will be very hot, and cook over medium-low heat for 45 minutes to 1 hour, uncovered, stirring and scraping the base and sides often, until the beef is very tender and the sauce has turned a deep brown that clings to the meat. Lower the heat if it starts to catch, and stir constantly during the last few minutes, as the thickened sauce can scorch on the base quickly once most of the liquid has gone. By this point the beef, braised far beyond 63°C, should be completely fork-tender.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Remove the lemongrass, lime leaves and cinnamon stick, then let the curry rest for 5 minutes. Scatter over the sliced lime leaf and serve with plain rice.

tips: Watch the pan closely during the final hob stage — as the sauce dries out it can catch on the base, so lower the heat and stir constantly once it starts clinging to the meat.
Make it a day ahead if you can; the spices settle deeper into the beef overnight and the sauce clings even better once reheated.
If the spice paste won't come together in the processor, add water only 1 tbsp at a time — too much will make the final sauce harder to reduce.
Stir every 30 minutes during the oven stage so the paste cooks evenly rather than catching around the edges of the dish.
This curry freezes well for up to 3 months and, as a dry curry, often reheats just as well as the day it was made.
storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour; use within 3 days and reheat only once until piping hot (74°C). It also freezes well for up to 3 months. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
